topic: Regasification throughput upgrade and Phase 2 expansion progress (2025-2026)
wiki_text: In April 2026, PV Gas reported a successful trial run that raised the Thi Vai terminal's regasification throughput to about 288 tonnes/hour (~9.5 million standard m3/day), up from the original design capacity of 171 t/h, to help meet peak power demand. This is an operational/peak optimization rather than a change to the terminal's nameplate import capacity. Separately, PV Gas advanced the Phase 2 expansion that would triple total nameplate import capacity to 3 mtpa (Phase 1 at 1 mtpa plus a 2 mtpa Phase 2); PV Gas's CEO said in 2025 the firm had 'basically' completed preparations and was ready to sign the Phase 2 EPC contract in late 2025. PV Gas has also flagged plans to deploy an FSRU at Vung Tau port between 2026 and 2029, raising total system regasification capacity to ~22 million Sm3/day.

topic: Floating receiving configuration and 2026 grid-connection milestone
wiki_text: Delta Offshore Energy's Bac Lieu LNG-to-power project pairs a 2 mtpa floating LNG import terminal with a 3,200 MW combined-cycle power plant in the Mekong Delta. The receiving solution is described as a floating configuration: a Jettyless Floating Terminal (JFT), a Self-installing Regas Platform (SRP), and a Floating Storage Unit (FSU), with scale-model testing of the JFT/SRP/FSU and an LNG carrier completed at MARIN (Maritime Research Institute Netherlands). On 10 March 2026, EVNNPT and Bac Lieu LNG Power Company signed a Principal Agreement on Grid Connection to evacuate power via a 500kV Bac Lieu - Thot Not line. The project was retained in an appendix to the Revised PDP8 (April 2025) with a possible 2025-2030 start window. It is described as Vietnam's first fully privately financed integrated LNG-to-power project.

topic: Revival in Revised PDP8 and PV Gas terminal sponsorship (2025)
wiki_text: Ha Tinh province has proposed an LNG-fired Vung Ang 3 power complex (1,500 MW to 2030, expanding to 3,000 MW from 2030) as a substitute for gas-fired projects that missed deadlines or were excluded from PDP8. PV Power (a Petrovietnam subsidiary) is the major investor in the power plant, while PV Gas (PetroVietnam Gas) is the investor for the associated Vung Ang LNG import terminal, with a planned annual capacity of 1-3 million tonnes. The Revised PDP8 (Decision 768, April 2025) lists a new 'LNG Vung Ang III' LNG-to-power project among newly added LNG projects (Ha Tinh, with a 2031-2035 horizon for the larger phase). As of early 2025 the investors said they were ready to deploy upon Prime Minister's approval; both the plant and terminal are in the provincial master plan to 2030.
